name: libvips
summary: Upstream libvips image-processing library compiled for browser WebAssembly with a pinned Emscripten adapter.

profiles.label: Browser Core
features: resize / thumbnail / colourspace / composite / convolution operations
TIFF / GIF / imagequant / quantizr / legacy PPM-Analyze-Radiance loaders removed
externalLibraries: GLib, mozjpeg, libpng, libwebp and required dependencies built by the pinned wasm-vips recipe
profiles.output: Smaller generic libvips JavaScript API for JPEG/PNG/WebP Browser-Kitty-style image workflows
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

profiles.label: Browser Full
features: JPEG / PNG / WebP / TIFF / GIF raster processing
resize / thumbnail / colourspace / composite / convolution operations
externalLibraries: GLib and image codec dependencies built by the pinned wasm-vips recipe
profiles.output: Generic libvips JavaScript API with JPEG/PNG/WebP plus TIFF/GIF support
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Use browser-core for JPEG/PNG/WebP by default; choose browser-full only when TIFF/GIF support is needed. Both expose the same upstream-style libvips API.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/libvips/browser-core/browser-libvips.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function resizeToJpeg(file, width = 640) {
  const vips = await WasmZooLibvips.loadHosted({
    baseUrl: "/vendor/libvips/browser-core/"
  });

  const input = vips.Image.newFromBuffer(new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()));
  const resized = input.resize(width / input.width);
  const output = resized.writeToBuffer(".jpg[Q=85]");
  resized.delete();
  input.delete();
  return output;
}
</script>
notes: browser-core is the recommended Browser-Kitty profile: JPEG/PNG/WebP only, with TIFF/GIF/imagequant/quantizr and legacy PPM/Analyze/Radiance loaders removed.
browser-full adds TIFF/GIF/imagequant while keeping the same JavaScript API.
Both profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP) because libvips uses pthreads.
The raw vips.js API is the primary distribution. browser-libvips.js is only a self-hosting convenience loader.
The browser adapter and both Emscripten/libvips compatibility patch heads are pinned to immutable commits.
AVIF/HEIC, JPEG XL, SVG/resvg and UltraHDR remain intentionally disabled in the 0.5.1 metadata patch release.

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Native builds can enable additional loaders, platform integrations and filesystem-backed workflows.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Exact upstream libvips release exposed through a pinned browser adapter with a deliberately reduced optional delegate set.

comparison.name: wasm-vips adapter
comparison.note: Used as the browser binding/build adapter only; WASM Zoo pins and packages the corresponding upstream libvips version itself.

notes: v0.5.1 is the first metadata-enabled libvips patch release for WASM Zoo v0.8.0: the WebAssembly feature set and upstream pin are unchanged while standalone SLSA provenance and CycloneDX SBOM assets are added to the release contract.
libvips is published as a library API rather than a synthetic CLI wrapper.
browser-core is designed as the practical small default for Browser-Kitty-style JPEG/PNG/WebP processing; browser-full is the compatibility profile for TIFF/GIF.
Both profiles keep libvips threaded demand-driven execution, so Pages/local hosting must provide cross-origin isolation.
Build output records raw and gzip sizes and compare-profiles.mjs writes a machine-readable and Markdown core-vs-full comparison once both profiles exist.
Release archives include the exact build recipe, source bundle and third-party license notices needed to audit the statically linked browser artifact.

referenceWasm.name: wasm-vips
referenceWasm.note: WASM Zoo uses a pinned wasm-vips adapter commit but independently pins and packages the upstream libvips release.

capabilityMatrix.note: Exposed through the pinned wasm-vips Embind adapter.
Removed from Core to reduce transfer size.
cgif/imagequant path is only built in Full.
Large optional delegate families intentionally excluded from both current profiles.
Both profiles require SharedArrayBuffer / cross-origin isolation.
Target-specific optimization enabled for browser builds.
Browser builds use MEMFS and byte-buffer APIs rather than host filesystem semantics.
